tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when the user wants to know...'), focuses on user intent ('is my cluster okay' questions) rather than implementation, explicitly lists trigger contexts (control-plane/node-health checks, latency/throttling spikes, even when the user doesn't name the subsystem), and clarifies scope boundaries (read-only, not remediation, contrasting with aws-eks-operations-review). It is a single dense paragraph but remains within the 'short paragraph' allowance given the need to disambiguate from a similarly-named sibling skill.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill when the user wants to know whether an Amazon EKS cluster is healthy right now, or asks you to assess, triage, or report on the state of an EKS cluster... Reach for it for \"is my cluster okay\" questions, control-plane or node-health checks, and latency/throttling spikes; it only reads state and does not remediate."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but every section is specific to EKS health grading procedures, tool usage, and check IDs — it does not explain general concepts the agent already knows (e.g., what EKS or kubectl are). It jumps straight into domain-specific workflow and conventions.
tests.evidence: Grade the CP1–CP11 + CP-M1–CP-M9 from references/control-plane-health.md ... Apply the grading guards ... before fixing any verdict

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, metric thresholds, or error-code lists are embedded in the body; all detailed material (thresholds, queries, remediations) is delegated to references/ files and linked conditionally.
tests.evidence: Evaluate against references/thresholds.md ... Apply the grading guards in references/grading-guards.md before fixing any verdict

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown links either in the workflow steps or in the Reference files table.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link in the table and in the workflow text specifies a condition or trigger for loading it (e.g., grading a specific check series, or when a specific tool call fails).
tests.evidence: | [`references/grading-guards.md`](references/grading-guards.md) | **Before fixing any CA/CP/CP-M/CPM/NH verdict** — the false-positive controls (FP1–FP12) ... |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consistency-critical operations (grading, guard application, tool-denial handling) are given exact, prescriptive instructions, while the findings-analysis step explicitly grants freedom to reason using the agent's own EKS knowledge rather than reciting canned text.
tests.evidence: reason* from the observed evidence (what it means, symptoms, ranked probable causes, cascade risk, confidence) using your own EKS knowledge; do not recite a canned definition

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The source-fallback order for metrics is explicitly prioritized rather than presented as equal options.
tests.evidence: follow the source-fallback order ... (CloudWatch → **Prometheus/AMP if detected (mandatory)** → raw API server `/metrics` via `use_kubectl get --raw /metrics` → N/A)

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable grading methodology (detect sources, grade by series, apply guards, validate, report) that applies to any cluster/account rather than describing one specific instance.
tests.evidence: Work through these steps in order — each depends on the ones before it ... Step 0: Confirm the cluster — pin down name, region, and account.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: Grading guards and constraints sections function as a gotchas section, calling out specific false-positive traps and edge cases the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: an empty query / no-datapoint result is *unknown*, never an automatic PASS (FP11); a 429 spike is not "scale the control plane" (FP6).
